<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title><jats:p>Let <jats:italic>X</jats:italic> be a real prehomogeneous vector space under a reductive group <jats:italic>G</jats:italic>, such that <jats:italic>X</jats:italic> is an absolutely spherical <jats:italic>G</jats:italic>-variety with affine open orbit. We define local zeta integrals that involve the integration of Schwartz–Bruhat functions on <jats:italic>X</jats:italic> against generalized matrix coefficients of admissible representations of <jats:inline-formula><jats:alternatives><jats:inline-graphic xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink" mime-subtype="png" xlink:href="S0027763022000216_inline1.png"/><jats:tex-math>
$G(\mathbb {R})$
</jats:tex-math></jats:alternatives></jats:inline-formula>, twisted by complex powers of relative invariants. We establish the convergence of these integrals in some range, the meromorphic continuation, as well as a functional equation in terms of abstract <jats:inline-formula><jats:alternatives><jats:inline-graphic xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink" mime-subtype="png" xlink:href="S0027763022000216_inline2.png"/><jats:tex-math>
$\gamma $
</jats:tex-math></jats:alternatives></jats:inline-formula>-factors. This subsumes the archimedean zeta integrals of Godement–Jacquet, those of Sato–Shintani (in the spherical case), and the previous works of Bopp–Rubenthaler. The proof of functional equations is based on Knop’s results on Capelli operators.</jats:p>
title: GENERALIZED ZETA INTEGRALS ON CERTAIN REAL PREHOMOGENEOUS VECTOR SPACES

items.abstract: <jats:title>Abstract</jats:title><jats:p>We examine some properties of the 2‐variable greedoid polynomial <jats:italic>f</jats:italic>(<jats:italic>G·,t,z</jats:italic>) when <jats:italic>G</jats:italic> is the branching greedoid associated to a rooted graph or a rooted directed graph. For rooted digraphs, we show a factoring property of <jats:italic>f</jats:italic>(<jats:italic>G·,t,z</jats:italic>) determines whether or not the rooted digraph has a directed cycle. © 1993 John Wiley & Sons, Inc.</jats:p>
title: On the greedoid polynomial for rooted graphs and rooted digraphs

items.abstract: <jats:p>We introduce a hook-length polynomial for rooted trees obtained by combining the classical hook-length statistic with q-integers and vertex depth. This polynomial extends the classical hook product and serves as a weighted enumerative invariant of rooted trees. We investigate its fundamental properties, establish recursive relations, and derive explicit formulas for several important families of rooted trees, including paths, stars, and caterpillar trees. We further study structural properties such as specialization, degree, and multiplicativity, and present computational evidence illustrating the behavior of the polynomial on small trees. These results provide a framework for studying q-weighted hook statistics and suggest several new directions in enumerative combinatorics.</jats:p>
title: <p>A Depth-Weighted Hook Polynomial for Rooted Trees</p>
